title: Holdback Carried by a Vehicle with Claims on Its Host Protection Enrolment
content:
What the Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment standing on a vehicle shows about claims is a valuation ground of its own. Two things are read off that enrolment over the rolling twenty-four months counted back from the handling date: the claims filed on it, and the total of the appraisals settled in that window.

| Claims filed on the enrolment in the window | Appraisals settled in the window | Holdback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 or more | any total | eight hundredths (0.08) |
| any number | more than 5000 USD in total | eight hundredths (0.08) |
| exactly 1 | 5000 USD or less in total | four hundredths (0.04) |
| any other case | — | none on this ground, a holdback rate of 0 |

As clauses: a vehicle whose host protection enrolment shows two or more claims filed in the rolling twenty-four months counted back from the handling date, or appraisals settled in that window totalling more than 5000 USD, carries a holdback of eight hundredths; one whose enrolment shows exactly one claim filed in that window with appraisals settled there totalling 5000 USD or less carries a holdback of four hundredths; and any other vehicle carries no holdback on this ground.

### How the two counts combine

The first clause is met by either of its limbs on its own: a vehicle with 2 claims filed and nothing appraised carries eight hundredths, and so does a vehicle with 1 claim filed whose appraisals in the window total 5200 USD. The four hundredths clause needs both of its conditions at once — exactly 1 claim filed and appraisals of 5000 USD or less — so a single claim appraised at exactly 5000 USD carries four hundredths, while the same claim appraised at 5000.01 USD carries eight hundredths.
